dev.cite: Product comes first. Product stories (a consumer actor, product value) rank above process, tooling and mob-internal cards.
dev.reply_head:
Support-it
The note matches the working agreement: product stories rank above process/tooling, only bugs with user-data/safety/shipping risk may sit above them, and process work is explicitly not board work. The proposal also preserves the head-size guard and the reversal path, and its closed/converted cards align with the product-owner ruling that process improvements are retro proposals, not issues. It is workable, fair, and reversible without gaming.

coach.cite: Only bugs that put user data, safety or the team's ability to ship at risk may sit above them
coach.reply_head:
Support-it
This note keeps the board product-first, preserves the bug guard, and makes the risk-based exception explicit. It recognizes that only 299 and 305 meet the stated bug rule, keeps product work ahead of process/tooling, and folds process cards into the product stories they serve. It also records the product-owner ruling and makes the head-size and reversal conditions clear, reducing churn without changing the board’s live scope. It is appropriately scoped and not padded.

coach.reply_head:
Support-it
This is well-scoped, product-first, and consistent with the working agreement’s Value and Product-first rules. It reduces ceremony by treating process work as retro/experiment items rather than board cards, and it keeps only the proven at-risk bugs above product work. I support the intent and the head-size guard, though the proposal still carries a few not-fully-verified judgments (for example some old blank-Type assignments and fold-ins), so I would not treat it as a full endorsement
